NONE: › a religious leader and teacher in the Jewish religion
拉比（猶太教領袖和經師）

example: Rabbi Jonathan Sacks
喬納森．薩克斯拉比
[ as form of address ] Good morning, Rabbi.
早安，拉比。

NONE: A2 a small animal with long ears and large front teeth that moves by jumping on its long back legs, or the meat of this animal eaten as food
兔，家兔

example: a pet rabbit
家兔寵物
See also
bunny

NONE: › to continue talking about something that is not interesting to the person you are talking to
沒完沒了地說；嘮叨；喋喋不休

example: He's always rabbiting on about his stamp collection.
他總是沒完沒了地說他的集郵。

NONE: › a large, noisy, uncontrolled group of people
烏合之衆；暴民
› people of a low social position
下等人；賤民

example: The defeated army returned home as a demoralized rabble.
這支失利的軍隊如烏合之衆一般失魂落魄地逃回了老家。
He views his opponents as a mindless rabble.
他視他的反對者們為一幫毫無頭腦的烏合之衆。
Her speech stirred the emotions of the rabble.
她的演講煽動起了下等人的情緒。

NONE: › a person who makes speeches that make people excited or angry, usually intentionally in order to make them act in a particular way
（尤指按自己的想法）煽動暴亂者，蠱惑人心者

example: Johnson was unpopular with the management because he was a well-known rabble-rouser.
管理層很不喜歡約翰遜，因為他是出了名的煽風點火者。

NONE: › the grain crop that is cut and collected in spring
早春作物
› suffering from rabies
患狂犬病的
› disapproving having and expressing extreme and unreasonable feelings
極端的；過激的；狂熱的

example: a rabid dog
瘋狗
The attack is believed to have been carried out by a group of rabid anti-semites.
據信，襲擊是一群狂熱的反猶分子所為。
Even the most rabid football fans probably wouldn't know this.
即使是最狂熱的足球迷也可能不知道這個。

NONE: › a serious disease of the nervous system that can cause death. Rabies can be passed on to humans by other animals.
狂犬病

example: Dogs, cats, foxes, and bats can all carry rabies.
狗、貓、狐狸和蝙蝠都可能傳播狂犬病。

NONE: › a skilful way of kicking a football, in which your kicking leg is directly behind your standing leg as you kick the ball forward
（足球）一種花式踢球術（踢球腿在支撐腿正後方）
